title: Reading One Pet's Usage from Shipments before a Household Rise on Tailwise Autoship
content:
When the household's usage rose in the last six months, the usage of the pet on an existing Tailwise Autoship being re-sized to its own pet's usage (a non-prescription Autoship that has been carrying food for more than one pet of the household) is read from the shipments before the rise.

## When usage rose

The usage rose when scheduled shipments were charged both in the last six months and between six and twelve months ago, and the average units per scheduled shipment charged in the last six months exceed the average units per scheduled shipment charged between six and twelve months ago. It did not rise when either period has no scheduled shipment.

A record counts as dated in the last N months when its date is later than the same calendar day N months before the day the value is worked out, so a record dated exactly N months earlier does not count; a record dated between six and twelve months ago is one dated in the last twelve months but not in the last six months.

## Usage read

| Usage rose | Scheduled shipments charged between six and twelve months ago | The existing pet's weekly usage |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 3 or more | The units of those shipments divided by 26 weeks |
| Yes | fewer than 3 | The units of those shipments divided by the product of their number and the subscription's weeks between shipments, so each of them is taken to have lasted one interval |
| No | — | Not read from the earlier shipments |

## Worked cases (hypothetical subscription on a 4-week frequency)

- Between six and twelve months ago: 4 scheduled shipments of 2 units (average 2); last six months: 5 of 3 units (average 3). Usage rose, 4 shipments is at least 3: 8 units divided by 26 weeks, about 0.31 unit a week.
- Between six and twelve months ago: 2 scheduled shipments of 2 units; last six months average 3. Usage rose, fewer than 3: 4 units divided by 2 shipments multiplied by 4 weeks, that is 4 divided by 8, 0.5 unit a week.
- Equal averages in both periods: not a rise.
